The codex is made up of fragments of various books bound together.  The Bede section is a single bifolium comprising ff. 87-88 of the current codex.  The text on fol. 87 is CTe II.11-12, from ch. 11 “... cum sederit filius hominis” to the end on 87r, and ch. 12 through “venit hora ...” on the verso.  Fol. 88 has ch 15 from “... patriae caelestis introducimur ...” to “studuerunt cor[poris]” on the recto, and continuing through “fulgerent, sed in eiusdem ...” on the verso. There is an AVG 240.5 words / side; with 2886 words omitted between the two leaves. 2886 / 240.5 = 12 exactly, which indicates that 6 leaves (12 sides) were between the two leaves of this bifolium, which in turn suggests that this bifolium was the outer leaf of a gathering of eight.  This assumption is confirmed by the quire mark “iiij” in the lower margin of 88v. 10,154 words / 61,601 chars. preceded the text preserved here in CTe.  That amount of text would fit on 42-43 sides = 22 leaves.  If we allow for a blank leaf and extra space for an initial and capitula, that would work well with an imagined 3 gatherings of 8 leaves preceding the gathering that originally contained this leaf. There are 15,210 words / 91,234 chars. of CTe following the last bit on 88v, enough text to fill an additional four regular gatherings after this.
